references.text: Jacob's sons demand that the people of Shechem be circumcised as a condition for marriage, illustrating circumcision's significance as an identity marker for the covenant people.
Any servant bought with money must be circumcised to eat the Passover lamb, demonstrating circumcision's role as entry into the covenant community.
Joshua circumcises the Israelites at Gilgal after the wilderness wanderings, restoring the covenant sign that God commanded Abraham.
Moses urges Israel to circumcise their hearts—a metaphorical use of circumcision symbolism to signify inner renewal and devotion to God.
God promises to circumcise the hearts of the Israelites and their descendants so that they will love Him wholeheartedly, offering a spiritual deepening of circumcision's meaning.
Jeremiah warns Judah to circumcise themselves for the Lord and remove the foreskins of their hearts—a metaphorical application of the physical covenant sign.
Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day, in accordance with the covenant command given to Abraham.
In Stephen's speech, reference is made to the covenant of circumcision that God gave Abraham, directly linked to the instruction regarding circumcision as a covenant sign.
Paul discusses the value of circumcision and states that a true Jew is circumcised in the heart by the Spirit—an expansion from the physical covenant sign to inner renewal.
Paul explains that Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness he already had through faith, clarifying the relationship between faith and the covenant sign.
Paul warns against relying on circumcision for salvation and emphasizes that in Christ Jesus, what matters is faith working through love.
Paul describes a circumcision not made with hands—the circumcision of Christ—as a spiritual fulfillment of the physical covenant sign.
Ezekiel expands on the concept of being brought under the bonds of the covenant as a dynamic response to the static covenant sign in Genesis.
This is the immediate context within the same covenant conversation where God's promise to establish the covenant is given before the sign itself (circumcision) is commanded.
Ezekiel proclaims the restoration of the eternal covenant initiated in Genesis 17, linking it to a new and deeper knowledge of God.
Leviticus 12:3 specifies the timeframe (the eighth day) for performing circumcision, which is defined as the sign of the covenant in Genesis 17:11.
The book of Hebrews connects the blood of the new covenant to the old covenant and offers a new understanding of what the 'sign' of the covenant (such as circumcision) truly points toward.
A direct parallel where the rainbow (Noah) and circumcision (Abraham) are both defined as the 'sign of the covenant' using identical language.
A theological parallel showing God's consistent initiative to establish covenants with humanity and their descendants.
